sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Compression Molding of Food-Grade Silicone Tactile Sensory Fidgets

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Republic of Panama; unitary national jurisdiction with no sub-state corporate or tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic codified system; the Private Interest Foundation is a hybrid statutory institution governed by special foundation law rather than general company law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (entered into force 1991)
Panama-United Kingdom Double Taxation Arrangement (in force)
Panama-Republic of Korea Double Taxation Agreement (in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT reform, Cabal system) Articles 230-238; Law 70 of 31 January 2019 (creation of the Unified Tax Information System and mandatory Beneficial Owner Registry); Executive Decree 753 of 30 September 2020 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales implementing rules, thresholds and tariffs); Law 42 of 2011 (terrorist financing asset freezing regime); Law 25 of 12 June 1995 as amended by Law 3 of 9 January 2017 (Private Interest Foundation statute and transparency obligations); Resolution 202 of 2017 of the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — the Beneficial Owner Registry is administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) under Executive Decree 753/2020; filings are not publicly searchable and are disclosed only to designated Panamanian competent authorities (DGI, Unidad de Análisis Financiero, Public Prosecutor's Office, courts) and to foreign authorities exclusively through lawful tax information exchange or mutual legal assistance channels.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of the Foundation Charter (Copia Certificada del Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Público de Panamá (Panama Public Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961, applicable to Panama) OR Consular Legalization at a Panamanian consulate where the destination state is not an Apostille Contracting State

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Registered Entity Certificate (Certificado de Persona Jurídica)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Público de Panamá (Panama Public Registry)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Panamanian Resident Agent (Poder Especial con Cláusula de Representación)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the jurisdiction of origin of the grantor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization at the competent Panamanian diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Declaración Jurada de Beneficiario Final) submitted to the DGI Beneficial Owner Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Resident Agent acting as fiduciary intermediary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization when the declaration is executed abroad or relied upon by a foreign regulated financial institution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based due diligence under Law 23 of 2015, Law 42 of 2011 and Executive Decree 753/2020: (i) identification of domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates; (ii) real-time screening against UN Security Council consolidated sanctions and Panamanian national asset-freeze lists maintained by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and the Consejo Nacional de Seguridad; (iii) screening against U.S. OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists as compulsory market practice in Panama's fully dollarized banking system; (iv) screening against EU CFSP consolidated lists and FATF high-risk jurisdiction countermeasures; (v) enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval required for any PEP or sanctions match; the registered agent must conduct refreshed screening at incorporation, upon any UBO change, and on an annual cycle.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección General de Registro de Personas Jurídicas y Valores (official portal: https://www.registropublico.gob.pa; online preliminar check via 'Mi Registro' where available, physical application for the name availability certificate otherwise required)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names must be submitted in Spanish or in a foreign language rendered in Latin-script characters; foreign-language names that equate to a prohibited Spanish token or that misrepresent the legal form may be rejected unless translated; the chosen name must incorporate the mandatory indicator 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or the abbreviation 'FIP'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An extension may be requested before expiry at the Dirección General de Registro de Personas Jurídicas; one additional 30-day reservation is generally granted upon payment of a further statutory fee. Upon formal rejection, the applicant may file a 'recurso de reconsideración' with the Director General within five business days, followed by a hierarchical appeal; further judicial review lies before the Contencioso-Administrativo chamber of the Corte Suprema de Justicia.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for administrative conduct of the foundation: a Private Interest Foundation is not required to maintain operational staff or physical premises in Panama, provided the licensed resident agent maintains a real registered office address in Panama where official notices and UBO records are kept; a mere letterbox at the agent's office satisfies the statutory registered-office requirement for a non-operating foundation holding fidget-toy manufacturing IP and receivables.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 10% probability of an unannounced physical inspection at the registered office within the first three years. The DGI and UAF conduct risk-based inspections only, and the ISIC 3240 food-grade silicone tactile fidget activity is classified as Low_Risk_Standard by the AML banking tier, materially reducing the likelihood of onsite supervision.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory annual fee applicable to Private Interest Foundations under Law 25 of 1995

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations (Ley 25 de 1995 sobre Fundaciones de Interés Privado), as amended by Law 41 of 2015 and Law 1 of 2018; applicable Articles 1-5, 8, 18, 22, 25-26 and 42-45.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Directorate of Private Interest Foundations (Dirección General de Fundaciones de Interés Privado), Ministry of Government and Constitutional Affairs (Ministerio de Gobierno y Asuntos Constitucionales), Republic of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Ficha de Inscripción (Foundation Registration Form) accompanied by the notarized Testimonio of the Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública / Carta Fundacional).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Law 25 of 1995 imposes no fixed statutory minimum, but the Foundation Charter must declare a realistic initial endowment; notarial and AML/CFT practice requires a stated initial endowment of at least USD 10,000, fully subscribed and evidenced by a bank deposit certificate. No State escrow account applies; the endowment is paid directly to the foundation bank account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, on this 12th day of the month of registration, by the Foundation Council of PA_PIF: (1) the Foundation Charter executed under Law 25 of 1995 is ratified and its initial endowment of USD 10,000 is accepted as fully subscribed, with title vested in the foundation for its stated purpose; (2) the registered office is adopted at the office of the Resident Agent in Panama City and registered with the General Directorate of Foundations; (3) the resident agent is appointed as registered agent; and (4) the undersigned Council members and Protector are confirmed in office, and the Council Chair is authorized to file the Charter, open bank accounts, and bind the foundation pending formal registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Legal Instruction and Drafting of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian Attorney (Abogado Idóneo) acting as Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder instructs the attorney, who drafts the Carta Fundacional in Spanish and English, including the foundation name, ISIC 3240 object clause, initial endowment, founder, Foundation Council members, Protector, registered office and resident agent; conflict-of-interest and KYC verification is completed.
required_dossiers: Original or authenticated copy of founder's passport
Proof of physical or registered address of founder
Signed KYC/AML questionnaire for founder, Council members and Protector
Statement of initial endowment and source of funds
Foundation purpose and object clause draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the foundation name conflicts with an existing registry entry, an alternative name is reserved and the Charter re-drafted; documentation defects are corrected and re-notarized without additional State fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder and Council members appear before the notary and execute the Escritura Pública in the presence of two attesting witnesses; the notary legalizes signatures, issues the notarized testimonio and returns the certified copy for registration.
required_dossiers: Passports of founder, Council members and Protector
Proof of payment of notarial fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary rectifies formal deficiencies by marginal amendment and re-issues a corrected testimonio for filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Foundation with the General Directorate of Foundations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Directorate of Private Interest Foundations, Ministerio de Gobierno y Asuntos Constitucionales
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Resident Agent files the Ficha de Inscripción, the notarized testimonio and the first Council resolution, and pays the USD 250 State fee through the national treasury; the Directorate issues the registered Foundation Certificate.
required_dossiers: Ficha de Inscripción signed by the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a prevención (query), the deficiency is cured and the file re-submitted within 15 business days; if time-barred, a fresh application with a new fee receipt is presented.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirmation of Registered Office and Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Resident Agent; General Directorate registry records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Resident Agent files the formal acceptance letter, certifies the registered office address, and updates the registry file; the foundation maintains its registered office ledger and the Resident Agent issues the certificate of legal personality.
required_dossiers: Lease or premises proof at the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the address is rejected, the Resident Agent substitutes an equivalent Panama City address and files a change-of-address notation with the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial Ownership and AML Filing with Fiscal Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Registro de Beneficiario Final; Compliance Officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Resident Agent compiles the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) register and files the sworn beneficial ownership statement with the DGI under Law 196 of 2019; the register is retained at the Resident Agent's office and updated within 30 days of any change.
required_dossiers: UBO identification and percentage of economic interest
Copy of the registered Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: An amended beneficial ownership return is accepted by the DGI; late-filing penalties are mitigated by voluntary correction before administrative notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating Notice and Industrial Activity Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of Panama (Alcaldía de Panamá) through the Single Window for Investment (Ventanilla Única de Inversión); MICI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foundation files the Aviso de Operación for industrial manufacturing of toys (ISIC 3240), obtains the municipal operating certificate and tax file, registers the industrial activity with MICI, and registers as employer with CSS and DGI if hiring staff.
required_dossiers: Lease contract for the production facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The applicant appeals a municipal objection within 30 days; the industrial classification and zoning certificate are corrected to remove the objection and the application is re-submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial Pre-Occupation Fire, Safety and Environmental Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foundation obtains the fire-safety certificate after on-site inspection, and submits the Category II Environmental Impact Study (EsIA) to MiAMBIENTE for issuance of the environmental operating permit before production begins.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Supplementary mitigation measures are incorporated into the EsIA and a new technical opinion is requested; fire-safety defects are corrected and a re-inspection is scheduled within 10 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce and Industries (MICI) — Directorate of Business Registration, through the Single Window for Investment (Ventanilla Única de Inversión)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación — Industrial Category (Municipal Operating Notice for Manufacture of Games and Toys, ISIC 3240) together with the MICI Industrial Activity Certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (Ministerio de Ambiente, MiAMBIENTE) — Department of Environmental Impact Assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II (moderate impact): small-footprint silicone compression molding facility requiring a registered Estudio de Impacto Ambiental (EsIA) under Executive Decree No. 123 of 2009; a Category I registration tier may apply if installed capacity is below 500 kW and floor area below 500 m²
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater to municipal sewer per Executive Decree No. 2 of 1982 (BOD5 ≤ 150 mg/L, TSS ≤ 150 mg/L, pH 6.0-8.5); VOC emissions from molding presses captured by local exhaust with activated-carbon filtration achieving at least 90% reduction; solid scrap silicone managed per Law 38 of 2017 waste hierarchy; food-grade silicone must comply with FDA 21 CFR 177.2600 and EU Regulation 10/2011 migration limits for leachable heavy metals (Pb, Cd, Hg), certified by an accredited laboratory under ASTM F963-17.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-prevention certificate (Certificado de Prevención de Incendios) from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; municipal construction-office structural load certification before occupancy; workplace hygiene clearance from the Ministry of Health (DIGESA); and occupational health-and-safety program compliance with MITRADEL, including emergency evacuation plan, noise control, first-aid provisions and worker exposure monitoring.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama's national tax administration; e-filing portal: Sede Electrónica / e-Tax Panama (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa). Export customs clearance is administered by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) through the Ventanilla Única de Comercio Exterior (VUCE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Private Interest Foundation (PIF): (1) appoint a licensed Panamanian attorney/resident agent; (2) register the PIF instrument at the Registro Público under Law 25 of 1995; (3) if the PIF will carry on any Panamanian-source commercial activity or export sales, file the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) application with the DGI within 30 days of commencement, submitting the registered foundation instrument, resident-agent acceptance, founder/council identification and the CIIU/ISIC 3240 activity code; (4) obtain an electronic signature and activate the DGI Sede Electrónica taxpayer profile; (5) obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación and register in the ANA/VUCE exporter database; (6) a purely passive PIF holding offshore assets requires no RUC or ISR/ITBMS registration, but the annual foundation annuity to the Public Registry/Treasury must be paid to maintain legal good standing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election regime. Available elections: (a) foundation-instrument election to limit the PIF to passive offshore asset holding, keeping it outside Panamanian territorial ISR/ITBMS taxation; (b) voluntary election to register as an ITBMS general-regime taxpayer to access export zero-rating and input-credit refunds; (c) simplified small-taxpayer election (Law 88 of 2010) for local gross receipts up to B/.36,000 per year, replacing ISR and ITBMS with a single 2%-5% tributo único; and (d) mandatory territorial sourcing — no election exists to tax foreign-source income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — Panama's VAT-type tax under Articles 1057-A et seq. of the Código Fiscal, administered by the DGI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general de-minimis turnover threshold: any person habitually transferring taxable goods or rendering taxable services in Panama must register for ITBMS from the first taxable operation. A simplified small-taxpayer regime (single tax of 2%-5% on gross receipts) is available where annual gross income does not exceed B/.36,000 (Balboa at par with USD). Exporters are required to register under the general ITBMS regime even when they have no domestic taxable turnover, so as to lawfully claim the 0% export rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) under the DGI's e-Tax program, phased in by taxpayer segment (already binding for large and medium taxpayers). General-regime taxpayers must issue invoices through a DGI-accredited PSFE and transmit the invoice XML to the DGI Sede Electrónica clearance API in real time to obtain a digital validation stamp (QR/XML reference) before the invoice is delivered to the buyer. Export e-invoices must contain the ANA export declaration (DUA) number and the zero-rated export reason code. Invoices without the DGI validation code are invalid for ITBMS credits and cannot substantiate export zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: supplies of movable goods physically exported from Panama are zero-rated, provided the goods leave Panamanian customs territory through the ANA within the applicable export period and are covered by a valid DUA in the exporter's name. Services: services rendered to non-resident recipients without a Panamanian establishment are zero-rated as export services when the benefit is consumed wholly abroad, payment originates from foreign currency outside Panama, and the supplier is an ITBMS general-regime taxpayer. Input ITBMS attributable to zero-rated export activities is creditable and excess credits are refundable (devolución de saldo a favor) by the DGI; the exporter must file the periodic ITBMS return with the export schedule and maintain the complete documentary bundle. Although Panama is dollarized and imposes no statutory FX-repatriation rule, bankable practice requires the inward USD credit to appear within 180 days of export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera, DUA) electronically certified by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA), identifying the exporter's RUC, the HS/CIIU 3240 commodity code and the actual departure date from Panama
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued to the order of the Panamanian exporter, evidencing physical receipt, shipment and export of the silicone stress-relief fidget toys to the foreign consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice from a licensed Panamanian bank evidencing settlement in US Dollars (Balboa at par) by the foreign buyer within the 180-day documentary benchmark
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may re-assess zero-rated exports within the general 5-year limitation period (extended to 7 years for unregistered taxpayers). If export substantiation fails, the 7% ITBMS is clawed back retroactively together with: (i) surcharges of 10% (first 2 months), 20% (2–6 months) or 30% (beyond 6 months); (ii) compensatory interest; (iii) fines of B/.250–B/.10,000 for false or defective invoicing; and (iv) an evasion penalty of up to 100% of the omitted tax. Falsified DUAs, simulated exports, forged Bills of Lading or sham inward remittances are tax and customs fraud punishable by 2–5 years' imprisonment, RUC suspension, loss of refund rights and joint liability of the registered agent and the foundation council; previously refunded credits are recoverable with interest from the refund date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) – Panama does not maintain a distinct central bank; the SBP is the banking supervisor and FX compliance authority for licensed commercial banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized monetary system with zero exchange controls. Both the US dollar and national balboa circulate as legal tender. Capital account and current account transactions are freely convertible and reversible, with no surrender requirements, no movement restrictions, and no profit repatriation hurdles. Taxes may still apply on territorial source income, but there is no FX approval mechanism.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion rules exist under Panamanian law. Exporters may retain and freely dispose of foreign currency proceeds, typically through commercial banks.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI (electronic money institution) viability is Low-to-Medium. Panama does not yet have a dedicated EMI licensing regime, so foreign EMIs may only operate through locally licensed banks, trust companies, or payment processing partnerships. The SBP requires physical or risk-based compliance and does not grant standalone digital licenses to unregulated offshore EMIs.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and the foundation's economic-benefit owner are generally required to appear personally or through a designated representative before a notary for certified KYC, particularly for non-resident clients. A minority of banks permit remote opening with apostilled corporate documents, video interview, and a Panamanian legal opinion; however, physical presence in Panama is still recommended to avoid higher bank scrutiny and to expedite due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident Private Interest Foundation anonymity and UBO opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly certified foundation charter, registered appointment of the foundation council, notarized UBO declaration, CVs, and a legal opinion from a Panamanian attorney confirming the foundation's valid constitution and compliance with Law 25 of 1995.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for foundation capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements or certified bank statements of the grantor/founder, sale and purchase contracts, employment or dividend records, and signed letters explaining the economic rationale for the foundation's business purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low-risk sole-purpose fidget manufacturing not matching banking business profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Description of ISIC 3240 operations, pro-forma income projections, purchase orders from overseas buyers, and governmental industrial classification certificates where available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty jurisdictions with higher AML risk exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: KYB documentation on trade counterparties, a mitigated risk analysis, and a clear inventory of the target payment rails (SWIFT TT and Platform_Pay).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant injections are effected by SWIFT wire from the founding shareholder or parent entity to the PIF's operational or escrow bank account, with purpose code 'A1 – Direct Investment' or 'K1 – Capital Contribution' as accepted by the receiving Panamanian bank. The bank holds the foundation charter and board resolution on file and may require a source-of-funds declaration for high-value transfers. Marketplace receipts through 'Platform_Pay' are channeled as operating revenues into the same account once the marketplace settlement processor is registered with the bank; no separate exchange control approval is necessary.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier payments are cleared via SWIFT MT103 for open account, advance payment, and pre-shipment transactions, or by an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit for larger silicone procurement cycles. The paying bank requires underlying invoices, packing lists, transport documents, and the commercial purpose code corresponding to import of goods. Any Platform_Pay refunds or chargebacks are also executed via SWIFT MT103 using the appropriate general refund purpose code.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD-denominated accounts eliminate the need for local FX hedging; where CNY, EUR, or other trade currencies are involved, Panamanian banks offer deliverable currency forwards and cross-currency swaps to settle expected trade flows.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible for currencies subject to domestic transfer restrictions, notably the offshore CNY NDF market for Chinese silicone suppliers.
Foreign currency options and structured collars are available for large procurement cycles from tier 1 banks, though they are subject to client risk classification and credit limits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Maintenance Franchise Tax (Tasa Anual) - Registro Publico
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Publico de Panama (Public Registry of Panama), Foundations Section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 31 March for the current calendar year; the payment maintains the Foundation in good standing in the Public Registry.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 10% surcharge applies after 31 March; continued non-payment for successive years triggers administrative strike-off by the Public Registry and the suspension of the Foundation's legal standing until arrears, surcharges, and reinstatement fees are settled.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Declaracion Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI), Beneficial Ownership Registry, Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in the calendar month allocated under Executive Decree 56573 of 2022, based on the last digit of the Foundation's RUC or Registry file; any change in beneficial ownership must be reported to the DGI within 30 calendar days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of USD 5,000 to USD 50,000 per violation under Law 254 of 2021; the DGI may suspend the Foundation's RUC, withhold good-standing certificates, and impose additional restrictive measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaracion de Renta) - applicable only where the Foundation derives Panamanian-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI), Income Tax Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December fiscal year-end, the return is due on or before 15 March of the following year; for a DGI-approved non-calendar fiscal year, the return is due within three months after fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge of 10% of the tax due plus monthly inflation indexation; late-filing fines may be imposed, and the Foundation will not obtain a tax good-standing certificate (Paz y Salvo) until the return is filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registration of Charter Amendments (Foundation Charter amendments, Foundation Council member changes, Protector changes, registered agent transfers, and registered office changes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Publico de Panama, Foundations Section, through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: As-and-when changes occur; no annual deadline for unchanged Foundations, but documents must be presented to the Registry promptly after execution, with standard practice being within 20 working days of protocolization.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unregistered amendments are unenforceable against third parties; persistent failure to update the Registry file may prevent issuance of good-standing certificates and may contribute to administrative strike-off for cumulative non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit applies to Private Interest Foundations as a class. A certified audit is mandatory only if expressly required by the Foundation Charter, by the DGI under a regulated tax regime, by banking or financial-licensing authorities if the Foundation engages in regulated financial activity, or under the SEM law (Law 41 of 2007) if the Foundation holds a multinational headquarters license.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Foundations may maintain books under IFRS as issued by the IASB or under Panamanian local GAAP; IFRS is the accepted framework for banking, investment, and cross-border reporting and is presumed by the DGI for any Panamanian-source taxable operations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Foundation must file one annual beneficial-ownership confirmation with the DGI Beneficial Ownership Registry under Law 254 of 2021 and Executive Decree 56573 of 2022. The filing month is fixed by the entity's RUC or Registry file number, and any change in beneficial ownership, including indirect control through the Foundation Council or Protector, must be reported to the DGI within 30 calendar days. The registered agent must simultaneously refresh the Foundation's KYC file and retain supporting evidence for at least 7 years.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Founders and Beneficiaries (Foundation Charter and Foundation Regulations)
Register of Foundation Council Members and Protector
Minute Book of the Foundation Council

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 750 per year for licensed resident-agent and registered-office services in Panama City, excluding the USD 300 government fee and any notarization, translation, or apostille costs.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No audit is statutorily required for a passive asset-holding Private Interest Foundation; a voluntary IFRS financial statement compilation typically costs USD 800 - USD 1,800, while a full certified audit, when required by a founder, bank, or counterparty, typically costs USD 2,500 - USD 6,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial taxation model, exempting foreign-source income. Domestic manufacturing activities may benefit from a 15% reduced rate on the first USD 50,000 of taxable income for small taxpayers, a 5-year loss carryforward, and accelerated depreciation on qualified machinery. No withholding on export sales of fidget toys manufactured in Panama.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 222 (Declaración Jurada de Renta) filed electronically through the DGI online portal (Sistema de Declaraciones y Pagos / SID) operated by Panama's Dirección General de Ingresos.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., 31 March for a calendar year-end). A two-month extension is available upon formal request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue derived from Panama-source activities, including local sales of silicone fidget toys and services rendered in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero if all revenue is foreign-source. A Private Interest Foundation deriving only offshore income must file a nil return and separately disclose exempt foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions directly attributable to Panama-source income, including raw material costs, wages, depreciation, and permitted opex.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only deduct costs linked to Panama-source income. Foreign-source expenses should be excluded for nil-return purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deductions and exemptions. This is the base for applying the statutory rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Should be zero for a foundation with no Panama-source income or after exhaustion of loss carryforwards.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed corporate income tax at the 25% statutory rate on Box 3.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Leave zero when Box 3 is nil. Tax credits cannot generate a refund unless provided by law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance income tax payments, foreign tax credits, withholdings suffered, and statutory investment credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only credits genuinely sourced from Panama operations. Non-resident foundations typically have no such credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax due after application of credits and withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must equal zero in a nil return. Any tax due must be paid by wire transfer to the DGI identified collection account.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a surcharge of 10% of the tax due plus 1.5% monthly interest (or fraction thereof), capped at 50% of the tax. Additional fines under Tax Code Article 715 can reach USD 5,000. Criminal prosecution for willful non-filing can result in imprisonment of up to two years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid from Panama-source taxable profits. Undocumented share dividends are subject to a 20% effective rate at the corporate level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced dividend, interest, or royalty rate under a Panama double tax agreement (e.g., with Singapore, South Korea, Mexico, UAE), the beneficial owner must obtain a Panama Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and file a written application with the DGI using the official treaty relief request form, attaching a TRC from the counterparty jurisdiction and a beneficial ownership declaration. DGI approval must be obtained before making the remittance; retroactive refunds are generally unavailable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Panama-source royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to 15% withholding; interest paid to non-residents is also subject to 15% withholding. Treaty rates may reduce these to 5-10% depending on the applicable DTA and the recipient's beneficial ownership status.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 3,000,000 in related-party transactions per fiscal year triggers mandatory Local File / Master File documentation under Panama's transfer pricing rules; lower thresholds apply for transactions with entities in no-tax jurisdictions.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (Law 70 of 2019) apply. A Private Interest Foundation actively manufacturing silicone fidget toys in Panama must demonstrate adequate physical presence, qualified employees, local management, and core income-generating activities inside Panama. Failure to substance results in reclassification, fines, and removal from the registry.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally understating Panama-source revenue, fabricating invoices, claiming fictitious deductions, or falsely labeling domestic profit as foreign-source income to avoid CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty equal to 100% of the evaded tax, plus 10% surcharge, 1.5% monthly interest, and criminal fines under Panama Criminal Code Article 283; imprisonment of 2 to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members and directors are jointly and severally liable for evaded taxes when they order, participate in, or knowingly benefit from the evasion. Courts may order civil restitution, freeze personal assets, impose travel bans, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a PIF with no physical office, no employees, no local management, and no real business activity despite registration as a silicone fidget manufacturer, or misrepresenting substance to the ESR registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 70 of 2019, fines up to USD 1,000,000, mandatory dissolution, and strike-off from the Public Registry. The entity is reclassified as fully taxable in Panama on worldwide income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced if the foundation is a sham or alter ego. Directors and council members become personally liable for all unpaid taxes and fines; personal assets may be seized, and officers may be prohibited from leaving Panama pending resolution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared Profit Repatriation / Dividend WHT Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends from Panama-source profits to foreign shareholders or beneficiaries without withholding the 10% dividend tax, or fabricating loans to siphon profits tax-free.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The foundation is liable as withholding agent for the full 10% unpaid tax, plus a 50% penalty under Tax Code Article 769, interest at 1.5% monthly, and possible criminal prosecution for defrauding the fisc.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the dividend resolution or directed the payment are personally liable for the un-withheld amount. Courts may impose civil restitution, asset freezes, travel bans, and imprisonment of up to three years for willful non-compliance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving Swift/TT or platform-pay proceeds for fidget toy sales without performing customer due diligence, maintaining beneficiary records, or filing required suspicious transaction reports; integrating funds into the foundation account without a legitimate economic rationale.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 23 of 2015, fines up to USD 1,000,000 per violation, revocation of the foundation's banking arrangements, and dissolution for repeated offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members are strictly liable for AML compliance failures. Penalties include personal fines up to USD 1,000,000, disqualification from serving as directors, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 10 years for money laundering offenses.
